sources.title: Rios, Saban and Zheng (2022 online/2023 volume), Improving Match Rates in Dating Markets Through Assortment Optimization
sources.publication: Manufacturing & Service Operations Management 25(4), 1304-1323; published online 2022-04-07; volume 2023
sources.method_and_section: Sections 2.1-2.2 (platform/exposure), 4.1.2 (quasi-experiment May 2019), 7.1-7.3 (2020 market experiments), Tables 2-3 and Appendix D
sources.contribution: Platform private dataset observes 3-9 profiles offered per daily assortment, individual like/no-like on shown profiles, preferences/attributes, actual matches, session timing, backlogs and activity; 2019 change allowing inactive backlogs used as quasi-exogenous variation in matches to assess impact on subsequent likes. Two 2020 market-level algorithm changes, Houston Aug19-25 vs Austin/Dallas control, Austin Sep9-15 vs Houston/Dallas control; DID report +27.13% and +37.95% expected matches vs default partner algorithm; published paper's own estimates, not ours. Paper reports at least 3% reduction in subsequent like probability per extra recent match under authors' quasi-experiment and design assumptions.
sources.observed_values_source: Original paper PDF extracted text, page indices P6/P7/P14/P27-P31/P53-P54; original visual screenshot of P0 succeeded, later individual table screenshots returned cache miss, so values in Tables 2/20 come from PDF extracted text not a visually verified table image.
sources.strongest_control: Original platform default algorithm, within-market before/after with DID across 3 cities and pre-trend/placebo/leave-one-control tests in appendix; not identical populations or independent raw-data replication.
sources.independent_cohort_note: One proprietary US dating-app platform; secondary Rios/Torrico paper SRC055 may reuse same industry partner/cohort and is not independent replication.
sources.data_reuse_rights: Proprietary app NDA; license for individual logs NOT verified; no right to download or rehost assumed
sources.text_reuse_rights: Published research article accessible via institutional repository; full reproduction not authorized by citation alone
sources.limits: Treatment market assignment one city of three; DID depends on parallel trends/no meaningful market interference; little effective independent clustering; match means in-app reciprocal like, not contact exchange or couple longevity; exclusion of inactive profiles as IV may have exclusion/selections; estimates for short US market periods do not calibrate Spanish/Tinder/nonbinary populations, survival or public rejection reputation; no raw data/code verified.

sources.title: Arias-Sarah et al. (2024), Aligning the smiles of dating dyads causally increases attraction, PNAS
sources.what_it_contributes: Original paper PDF text pp 2, 3, 7, 8: 31 single heterosexual volunteers age 20-27 in 60 video speed-date dyads, 4 × 4-minute dates each, round-robin batches, crossed manipulated increase/decrease perceived partner smiles (two congruent, two incongruent), pre/post 7-point ratings, social relation model controlling actor and partner factors. Authors report strongest attraction effect in both-increased smiles relative incongruent mixed, not generic temporal synchrony; manipulation is constant offset rather than time-series synchronization. Author-reported chi-square interaction χ²(3)=9.7 P=.001 and multiple comparison d>.55.
sources.limits: Sample 31 clustered volunteers, small, heterosexual/video-only, subjective rating not actual stable relationship; no own replication. Video filter levels changed permanently over each 4 minute date, not dynamically synchronized expressions. Original χ²(3)=9.7 P=.001 is numerically inconsistent for df3: chi2_sf(9.7,3)≈.0213; df1≈.00184; adjacent independent test χ²(3)=.77 P=.37 similarly appears df misprint. Treat as a potential reporting inconsistency requiring author/source verification, not refutation or identified error of code.
sources.data_reuse_rights: Public article CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 applies to article, separate participant-level archival data rights unverified; no participant records rehosted.
sources.independent_study_note: This 2024 French video lab experiment distinct from Mixmosa and Columbia and the Rios platform; SRC057 references same experiment, not independent replication.
sources.falsifier: Repeat crossed increase/decrease smile manipulation, independently pre-registered, in broad consented sample with authentic bilateral acceptance and durable relationship follow-up; compare dyadic interaction effects to competent actor/partner and pre-attraction baselines.

sources.title: Arias-Sarah et al. GitHub original analysis scripts for 2024 PNAS smile manipulation experiment
sources.what_it_contributes: README and original R scripts behavior_GLMM_analysis.R (Git blob SHA 4e6d6476...) and synchrony_glmm.R (Git blob SHA 530e132d...) fetched via GitHub connector. sources.title: Luo, Liu, Peng, Ying and Zhang (2020), A Motif-Based Graph Neural Network to Reciprocal Recommendation for Online Dating, with original authors' public SSJY action graph
sources.source_inventory: sjjy_data/relations.csv, users.csv, train.txt, train_data.csv, test_data.csv, preference files, bundled code and pickle; pickle NEVER executed. Graph has 8,599,012 action records of which rec=8,366,058, click=184,291, msg=48,663; 59,921 users across all actions, 36,432 click/msg.
sources.what_it_supports: On click/msg-only graph, 232,954 events yield 177,413 unique directed arcs and 52 two-way click/msg dyads, arc reciprocity 0.0005862; 30 exact event-stub in/out-degree permutation null mean 0.00016746, max 0.00023428, Monte Carlo p-upper 1/31. Repaired after original code erroneously included rec, both original and repair commits saved. Source is independent of Columbia, Mixmosa, Rios and HCMST cohorts. Original paper studies network motifs/recommendation, so this is not an original new matching theory.
sources.critical_measurement: rec action meaning NOT VERIFIED; 8.366M rec excluded from primary. Reverse click/msg means two logged directed actions, not swipes accepted, match or durable relationship. 15k train and 3,750 test rows are artificially 50:50 balanced and correspond poorly to click/msg-only reciprocals; original labels were derived using reverse ANY edge. Not a clean independent predictive test, do not report AUC or rec-user effects.
sources.limits: Degree-only stub permutation ignores sex segregation, algorithms, opportunity sets, spatial/institutional constraints and temporal ordering; many edges are duplicates; 30 nulls give coarse Monte Carlo resolution; statistic not causal nor a test of ESBM superiority. No documentation of true exposures/nonclicked profiles or explicit declined candidates. Raw archive has no separate LICENSE in original GitHub; public authored link does not grant unqualified redistribution, keep aggregate-only publication and confirm consent terms for wider use.
sources.falsifier: Obtain codebook explicitly decoding rec and labels, timestamp and candidate exposure, then use truly matched risk sets, separable click/msg and degree+block-preserving null; independent external heldout and actual durable couples require further data.

sources.title: N82 original SSJY actor-target-ROUND-ACTION event data and audited within-slate action conversion
sources.contribution: Raw train.txt preserves user-specific ROUND lost in derived relations.csv. Authors' generate_graph.py explicitly exports only A/B/ACTION, discarding ROUND. On 8,366,058 unique user-target-round rec events, 165,703 have click same round (1.980658%) and 22,979 have msg same round (0.274669%). 92.024% distinct click triples and 49.541% distinct msg triples match rec. Test actors 3004 disjoint (1,705,093 rec offers) get heldout target-smoothed CTR logloss .0877533 vs global .0953849, improvement .00763165; actor-bootstrap 95% interval [.00697562,.00847595], B100; potential target heterogeneity predictive, no causal interpretation. 42.07% same dyad repeat rec, with first vs repeat click rates 2.49% vs 1.28%, selection-biased.
sources.limits: Same original archive and sample as SRC059, not a second independent cohort. Source author's precise rec semantics beyond related 2019 paper not verified and no proof rendered/attended recommendation; CLICK is profile visit not yes/like, MSG is outgoing message not match; absent click not explicit dislike; ROUND is actor-session index not synchronized calendar. Group/user-specific baseline stronger than global not tested prospectively; holdout actor is internal not external; repeated exposure comparison noncausal. Consent, standalone license and redistribution permissions not separately verified; data original not uploaded.
sources.contribution_to_novelty: Demonstrates practical instrument for observed recommendation-stage profiling and predictive target differences in existing dataset, not scientifically original phenomenon over earlier Su/Hu 2019 and Hitsch 2010.
sources.falsifier: Stronger within-slate group+round+target popularity baseline, true rendered/attended impression and randomized ranking, replicated separately, explicit rejection and lasting union outcomes.

sources.title: Charlot Franssen (2023), Predicting the Probability of a Relationship Breakup Using 7-Year Longitudinal Data: A Survival Analysis Approach — Tilburg University undergraduate thesis
sources.access: Full original university repository PDF original indexed text (26 pages) inspected. web screenshots pages 0,10,16 failed CACHE MISS; tables extracted as text only. No author's analysis code or data rows read, results not reproduced.
sources.contribution: Published thesis already merged HCMST 2009 waves1-6 (2009–2017) on caseid_new: 4002 total, 3009 baseline partnered. Survival prediction with Cox proportional hazards, Random Survival Forest (RSF) and DeepHit, 70/30 split; author-reported C-index: Cox .791, RSF .795, DeepHit .780; IBS Cox .087, RSF .085, DeepHit .090. Therefore 'using survival analysis/RSF on HCMST 2009 to predict breakup' has pre-2026 prior art. Related risk: thesis reports some Brier scores for 2017 as 3.387/3.149/1.500, >1, mathematically impossible for ordinary unscaled per-row squared error on binary outcomes; require verify unit/scale/transcription, do not claim invalidity without code and original source. Event time constructed from annual survey and if no breakups 2012/2016 assigned 2017 in figure, raises inspection needs. Use as prior art and weak comparative baseline; not causal ESBM validation.
sources.baseline: Cox PH, RSF, DeepHit with comparable baseline predictors; even these cannot identify app cause or formation/rejection stage; stronger survival analysis must account for baseline duration and competing death, proper holdout and evaluation.
sources.limitations: Student undergraduate thesis, not peer-reviewed causal replication. Scanned/indexed PDF pages not visual-confirmed due cache; C-index differences tiny, no uncertainty of difference replicated; modeling and preprocessing choices require adversarial audit. Same HCMST2009 survey as SRC067 et al — no new independent cohort.

sources.falsifier: Acquire actual full source and valid legal license, prereg cohort-and-duration model with interval censorship, death competing risk, weights and unknown attrition, compare preexisting strong Cox RSF DeepHit in proper separate time/platform holdout.

sources.rights: Scientific Use License v1 level 1 per-file; authentication and license acceptance mandatory; cannot assume model has consent or credentials. Public codebook CC BY4, data not CC BY4.

sources.title: Joel, Eastwick & Finkel: Is romantic desire predictable? two independent speed dating studies 2005/2007
sources.contribution: UK Data Archive DOI 10.5255/UKDA-SN-852716 original samples 163 undergraduates at 7 speed dating events in 2005, 187 at 8 events in 2007, four-minute observed meetings, >100 predate traits/preferences; prior random forest predicts actor 4-18% and partner 7-27% variance but not relationship-specific attraction residual. Data.zip ~1MB registered users only under UK Data Service End User Licence; codebooks.zip 79 KB and syntax.zip 12 KB public.
sources.limits: Two samples are separate years but part of same published research program, not Columbia or Mixmosa. Registered user authentication/terms not satisfied; no original data bytes, no SHA256 or binary bilateral acceptance/duration confirmed. Strong prior art against claiming predictive pair-specific compatibility from self-reports.
sources.rights: UKDS safeguarded registered-user End User Licence; access needs user's own registration and license acceptance, no circumvention.

sources.title: Eastwick et al. (2025) and Moreno et al. (2026): 4,542 Tawkify blind dates 2023-24, original dyadic reports and OSF deposition claim
sources.contribution: 2025 preregistered PNAS paper Eastwick et al. documents Tawkify N6262 participants and N4542 blind dates Oct2023-Jan2024, 9084 postdate reports (two per date), partner age and initial romantic desire. Participants ages 22–85, mean46.8, 4286 only one date, repeated daters. Contrary to simple age-hypergamy preference interpretation, authors find slight preference for younger partner with no gender difference in initial attraction. Moreno et al. 2026 reuse same EXACT Tawkify cohort to compare in-person and virtual first dates and state 'data and materials posted on OSF' at supplied view-only link. The OSF page failed web tool fetch; files, license, bytes and SHA not verified. Two papers are not independent replications; data same operator, dates and individuals.
sources.limits: Observed postdate desire is not explicit bilateral yes/no acceptance unless codebook proves, not actual union/duration. Matching is arranged by paid service, nonrandom selection into clients vs members, age range and self-reported postdate outcomes; conditional-on-date inference not unconditional preferences. Published 2025 age result and 2026 modality result are strong prior art. No OSF data retrieved and no terms verified, no novel test.
sources.rights: OSF data deposition stated by 2026 authors, but individual OSF file licenses, consent, ethics and sharing conditions unverified due inaccessible view-only page; cannot treat as CC BY.
sources.new_independent_sample: YES Tawkify cohort independent from Graz Joel Mixmosa Columbia, but 2025 and 2026 papers share same sample

sources.title: Pronk & Denissen (2020), A Rejection Mind-Set: Choice Overload in Online Dating — Study 2 original replication dataset
sources.contribution: The Tilburg University publisher record identifies authors' original replication deposit with three studies. Study 2 involved 158 analyzed people (82 male/76 female) judging photos of actually available participants, recording an explicit yes/no per offered profile, reciprocal match eligibility and order of opportunities. Published article reports mean 2.15 mutual matches/person and declining selectivity/matches for a subset; NOT recalculated here. Provides directly relevant prior art on choice overload and reciprocal choice, and a DIFFERENT original-data archive discovery route from Graz/UKDS/OSF.
sources.limits: B2FIND catalog metadata explicitly says restrictedAccess and OpenAccess=false; original bytes, row schema, licenses, consent for secondary reuse, participant-level bilateral joins, SHA256, and independent platform holdout NOT inspected. Real partner availability is documented, but pair-level ordering and full risk set for both sides require data audit. Not evidence of union/duration or causal contemporary-app effect.
sources.rights: Data and article rights separate. B2FIND info:eu-repo/semantics/restrictedAccess. No license accepted, authorization obtained, or data downloaded. Any future access must be legally authorized by user or archive.
sources.falsifier: Authorized archived file + actual binary yes/no joined pairs, eligibility/order documentation and independent event/person split; preregister a truly novel contrast beyond published rejection mind-set before outcomes.

sources.title: Ogushi, Azuma, Ishii & Miyata (2026), Predicting female and male participants' contact-exchange decisions from time-segmented multimodal behavioral features in speed dating
sources.contribution: Peer-reviewed paper published 2026-09-23 analyzes 625 observed speed-date interactions, including 619 with a male and female contact-exchange decision jointly observed. Original reported 2x2 table: both no 214, female-only yes 105, male-only yes 220, both yes 80; no independent microdata analysis here. Authors report RF classifiers using multimodal temporal behavior, weighted F1 female .6248 and male .5379, differences vs random baseline uncertainty includes zero. Material new contemporaneous prior art for binary bilateral end-of-date decisions and temporal behavioral controls, unlike mere ratings of desire or unverified platform clicks.
sources.limits: Published aggregated contingency table is NOT 619 downloadable row records; 2026 authors explicitly state data availability as article/supplements and invite inquiries. Participant-level raw outcomes, licensing, independent holdout, event split and stable-union follow-up NOT verified. Current study 619 pairs within one cohort, not 619 independent people nor 2026 validation of ESBM.
sources.rights: Paper CC BY; participant-level data availability and reuse licensing not verified. No author contacts permitted without user's explicit approval and none attempted.
sources.falsifier: Legitimately licensed original microdata with raw pairwise event decisions and novel preregistered prediction beyond published RF controls, tested on independent event/person cohort.

sources.title: Cabrera-Quiros et al. 2018 MatchNMingle original speed-date and mingle events, Delft University of Technology
sources.contribution: Independently collected human 3-event round-robin dating corpus: 92 participants (46 male/46 female), first event 16 each and two events 15 each, 3-minute face-to-face encounters with immediately documented interest ratings and social interaction sensors, followed by mingle. Official original author site documents 0–7 after-date scores for desire to see again, potential friendship/sexual/romantic partner, plus pre-date HEXACO and physical opportunities via rotation. MatchNMingle EULA establishes a concrete legal non-commercial scientific access route requiring user identification/signature and credential request, rather than anonymous unlicensed reuse.
sources.limits: Official date response fields are rating-scale 0–7, NOT a verified yes/no accept/reject for both actors. No observation of couple formation or duration. Mingle captures different uncontrolled non-romantic opportunities and should not be conflated with assigned dates. Random rotation within events is not proof of randomized person-selection or representativeness. Only 3 events imply weak event-level holdout and no platform-level external sample. Original files, row pairing, rights confirmation, file hash, exposure ids, missingness and disclosure limitations not checked. 4TU Mingle repository is related same participant cohort, not independent replication.
sources.rights: Original TU Delft host says EULA, academic noncommercial use after identification and signed agreement, username/password requested; third-party 4TU listing Restrictive Licence. Not accepted, no author approached. Article and dataset rights distinct; no access or redistribution authorization established.
sources.falsifier: Researcher signs/obtains explicit EULA access without assistant impersonation, obtains original file SHA256 and both participant keys; verify whether yes/no options exist separate from 0–7 ratings, pre-exposure covariates, and overlap across three events. Until then NOT an N83-ready binary reciprocal outcome.

sources.title: MultiMediate'24 Speed Dating corpus: video-call romantic meetings and mutual contact-sharing questionnaires
sources.contribution: Original challenge provider describes 227 online-video speed dates across 102 distinct people (51 male/51 female), approximately 6 minutes per date; survey consent, pre-date personality/empathy, seven postdate 1–7 impression items including interest in counterpart contact information; organizer may connect parties conditional on mutual interest. This is a separate observed interaction cohort from Delft MatchNMingle, Columbia, Graz, Pronk, Ogushi and Tawkify, not a derived mirror.
sources.limits: Public official 2024 page describes intended challenge validation sets and survey responses; no verified currently downloadable original row-level bilateral dataset or joint yes/no contact fields. Contact interest item is ordinal 1–7, not inherently an explicit binary yes/no; conditions for actual contact transmission, timestamps, participant/event crosswalk, files, holdout and attrition not inspected. Neither stable union nor duration measured in public description. A challenge evaluation subset is not automatically original full cohort or independent holdout.
sources.rights: Website documents GDPR-related participant consent for collection, NOT explicit secondary research reuse license for outside users. No license accepted, no data or recordings fetched, no authors contacted.
sources.falsifier: Locate legally authorized institutional release that identifies both paired decisions and observed offered pairs, participant identifiers, temporal ordering, privacy and terms; SHA256 original file plus design under strong prior-art controls before outcomes.

sources.title: Baxter et al. (2022), Initial impressions of compatibility and mate value predict later dating and romantic interest
sources.contribution: Authors report 3 original speed-dating studies, N=559 respondents and more than 6600 encounters, reciprocal binary yes choices after actual meetings, plus followups of matched pairs. Studies 1 and 2 Northwestern speed dating include 2005/2007 collections; third study was Anime North 2015 Toronto, in which the after-date yes/no produced mutual matches and 12 weekly followup surveys track further contact/romantic initiation. Social Relations Model separates actor's general desire, target partner consensus and relationship-specific attraction: partner and relationship effects predicted later contact and romantic involvement in authors' original meta-analyses. Independent of this project's code and novel scientific-prior-art gate for ESBM claims about first-meeting match and subsequent courtship.
sources.independence_caveat: Two Northwestern 2005/2007 component cohorts appear to overlap historically with SRC084 Joel/Eastwick/Finkel speed dating archives; do not call all three entirely new independent cohorts or independent corroboration without participant/event matching. 2015 Anime North is a distinct collection, but reused by an earlier publication noted in article. Three components in one paper are not automatically three independently acquired new datasets for project.
sources.rights: PNAS paper CC BY4, not automatic license for participant-level Excel; authors state deposit in OSF 10.17605/OSF.IO/3ZYN6. Explicit user rule forbids repeating OSF web/API attempts: did not attempt them. No alternative independently verifiable authorized raw file identified, no SHA256 or original rows.
sources.limitations: Source report not our replication or causal estimate. Followup is conditional on initial mutual match and thus selected; association cannot identify causal effect of initial romantic attraction or prove durable stable unions. 2015 festival sample selection and differences in gender/orientation and calendar across cohorts challenge transport. No independent ESBM holdout run, no novelty by repeating social relations model.
sources.falsifier: Acquire legally licensed original paired yes/no and follow-up records with data-specific rights and stable event IDs via a permitted new route; freeze distinct mechanistic claim and competent SRM/partner/actor controls plus independent cohort holdout before reading outcomes.

sources.title: Matz, Peters, Cerf et al. (2026), Large language models can detect verbal indicators of romantic attraction
sources.contribution: Published research evaluated 964 transcripts with identifiable speed-date endpoints and compared LLM judgments with human observers and the dater's own estimates; r about 0.12–0.23 for predicted date outcomes in original study. Historical parent event: 1,039 dates from 187 undergraduates (93 women, 94 men) participating in eight 2007 Northwestern speed-dating events, of which 964 were linked to transcripts. Authors refer to actual mutual exchanges of contact information; more detailed language/behavior baselines already exist for match prediction.
sources.independence_caveat: The exact published 187 participants and eight 2007 events match metadata of SRC084 Joel/Eastwick/Finkel's 2007 study. Treat as strongly likely SAME Northwestern source cohort, not new independent sample, pending raw ID/event audit. Baxter 2022 also includes Northwestern cohorts with probable overlap. This article is new prior art of model evaluation, not novel human-data source in this project.
sources.rights: Article CC BY licensing does not establish microdata/transcript/video rights. Project materials stated to be on OSF, which has not been contacted in this continuation; no legal reuse license for transcripts or videos authenticated.
sources.limitations: Prediction r is association; no intervention on language, randomization of who speaks to whom, original external test against new people or independent platform verified. Published internal splits should not be confused with independent study; LLM familiarity with pre-2007 language may be a transport concern but no own test.
sources.falsifier: Novel temporal dyadic language claim needs new consented and rights-cleared corpus with independent actors, sessions and external venue plus strong human, SRM, LIWC, RF and language baselines, prereg and code hash pre-outcome.

sources.title: Humberg, Gerlach, Franke-Prasse, Geukes and Back (2023), Date me for Science original 2015 Münster speed-dating cohort, PsychArchives package public-use CC BY 4.0
sources.contribution: PsychArchives record confirms a single original data+code+codebook supplementary ZIP under Sharing Level 0 (Public Use), CC BY 4.0; size 4.1 MB and publisher-provided MD5 97a7f6cdecbe65e6d82776da33a02158 (metadata only, not calculated SHA256). Original 2015 Münster Date me for Science study recruited 397 heterosexual singles and 940 in-person date dyads at 42 laboratory events; partners rotated within event; participants supplied post-date attraction/fit/likeability/interest/sexual attraction items rated 1–7. Full codebook and preprocessed data described in package, so novel explicitly open institutional acquisition route with many event clusters rather than Graz Scientific Use License or prior restricted archives.
sources.rights: PsychArchives archive identifies the ZIP itself as CC BY 4.0 Public Use Level 0; this is an explicit data-package license, not mere journal CC. Platform states Level 0 immediate public use. No per-user contract accepted, no author contacted. Do not redistribute person-level rows or reidentify participants.
sources.limits: Original ZIP direct download at pada.psycharchives.org returned HTTP 502 through public browse, and subsequent single direct transfer attempt failed. No fallback fetch loop. Published paper and archive list ordinal romantic attraction and date quality, not confirmed explicit yes/no for both actors in included prepared file. Dataset preprocessed for one paper may omit match/contact variable even if broader Date me for Science collected one. No actual codebook, raw entries, participants, outcomes or SHA256 accessed. Holdout by distinct 42 events would be within same recruitment frame, not external replication; public article explicitly acknowledges dataset used in other studies, so novelty needs dedup/prior-art check without OSF browsing.
sources.next_gate: Authorized transfer of original ZIP and verified SHA256, then non-outcome schema/codebook check for two native binary decisions with participant IDs and encounter-level exposures; no N83 until novelty A–J pre-outcome frozen and external cohort holdout. If only 1–7 post-date ratings, exclude strict bilateral claim.

sources.title: Zhao, Sidari, Lee and Zietsch (2024 online, 2025 issue), original 2014–2019 Queensland speed-dating dataset and permutation-baseline replication code
sources.contribution: Original Queensland ethical speed-dating research 2014–2019, article Study 1 n=1145 participants (not 1145 dyads), with analysis and permutation tests addressing stated vs revealed preferences; authors conclude omnibus preference tests can yield statistical artifacts. Original author public GitHub repository verified directly via connected GitHub tool. File Analyses/2014-2019 Speed Dating Data.csv exists (403,595 bytes repository metadata), and header-only read reveals id, partnerid, sessionid, sex, predate preference variables and postdate scalar attraction/trait judgments (goattrac and similar). This is a distinct original participant collection from Columbia, Münster, Northwest, MatchNMingle, and Australian samples already recorded if not explicitly deduped by IDs, no data rows inspected. Strong competent null for any ESBM claim that stated preferences translate to observed matching.
sources.rights: Article CC BY4; Github repo root has README.md and dirs Analyses/ and Simulations/ but no top-level LICENSE file, and public Github visibility does NOT by itself prove reusable dataset rights. No rights assertion beyond public access; no authors contacted, no terms accepted, no person-level data disclosed.
sources.limits: Header comprises id, partnerid and sessionid but no explicit yes/no choice, partner yes/no or mutual match column; there may be other files not inspected, so absence in examined published CSV does not prove source design collected none. Scalar attraction is not a binary behavioral decision; do not impose threshold. GIT blob SHA is Git object SHA1, not raw content SHA256 and not evidence of a downloaded original file. No original dataset rows, matching/union outcome, scientific model, code execution or external holdout verified. Open article and existing public code do not establish novelty for ESBM.
sources.next_gate: Check legal data reuse terms and original unreduced data/codebook for two measured binary decisions; require SHA256 of original bytes, nonoverlapping independent validation and frozen A–J+code before outcomes; otherwise use as only prior art / methodology control.

sources.title: Chang, Kragness, Tsou, Bosnyak, Thiede and Trainor (2021), Body sway predicts romantic interest in speed dating, McMaster LIVELab
sources.contribution: Distinct original McMaster Hamilton real face-to-face speed-dating two-session collection recruited 55 singles, with n=54 usable after missing female responses (authors), ~15 rounds per session, 4-minute dates. After each observed encounter both participants filled private native yes/no MeetingAgain 'Would you like to see this person again for a second date?'; when both answered yes contacts exchanged within 24 h. Critically the paper documents that 30/54 participants had inconsistent ordinal 9-point 'How interested in a second date' vs their native binary yes/no: direct external empirical evidence against treating Likert attraction as observed acceptance. Authors analyze body sway Granger directionality and groovy vs low groove music and actor/dyad mixed-effects as prior art.
sources.rights: Article CC BY 4.0 does not establish raw motion capture or response microdata license. The original authors' data availability says analyzed datasets only on OSF, raw time series via reasonable request and agreement. Per explicit user prohibition no OSF web/API attempt and no author contact or agreement accepted. Supplementary ZIP linked through article is not presumed to contain original pairwise decision rows or license.
sources.limits: Only two event clusters, different cohorts required to validate external predictions. Participant count 55 initially, 54 usable; observed dates not equated to observed stable unions or duration. Per-author yes/no responses confirmed by published method, not raw linked original fields. Raw rights, id and meeting crosswalk, codebook, event/round holdout, SHA256, data schema all unverified; data route via OSF blocked by prior instruction. Observed association body sway does not identify causal effect of coupling. Order of music shared by all subjects can confound music inference; no own reanalysis.
sources.falsifier: Acquire data only through a newly permitted and rights-verified original public alternative (not OSF, author request, or controlled content); verify original bytes SHA256, exact native two binary decisions and round exposure IDs, code prereg A–J before outcomes; require external independent cohort beyond the two sessions and stronger movement/actor/event baselines.

sources.title: Shahvali, Mitas, Ward and Boode (2024), Five Minutes to Love, BUas original cross-country speed-dating physiology and questionnaire dataset
sources.contribution: Independent original cross-national study from Breda University of Applied Sciences, Brigham Young University USA and Sun Yat-Sen University China: over 1000 observed brief speed dates according to host university, self-disclosure topics manipulated and physiological synchrony recorded. Researchers register data and accompanying materials for a SUBSECTION via Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13927395, listed by original BUas research portal as Rawdata participant physiology/times/metadata/questionnaires, MATLAB/R scripts and processed physiology. Cross-country contexts could enable external venue and culture stress tests if the original data actually expose paired decisions, overlap and legal rights.
sources.rights: Institutional page links to Zenodo DOI and describes files, but record-specific license/access status NOT verified. General Zenodo default CC BY4 is not legal evidence for this specific record; user explicitly prohibits accepting terms. Public institutional description is not evidence of participant consent for reuse of individually reidentifiable physiology, so do not download original participant folders until license & privacy terms verified.
sources.limits: The >1000 events refers to overall multi-institutional research PROJECT, not size of Zenodo subsection. Original record and API responded inaccessible to web service once each; do not retry blocked routes. The depositor lists questionnaires but no complete original codebook, paired explicit two yes/no/accept/decline, actual response rows, subject ids, original SHA256, data-specific license or usable external holdout inspected. Self-reported 'interest in future date' not necessarily native binary choice; cross-national sites may differ by design and data released. No claim of controlled effect with original data.
sources.falsifier: New, nonrepetitive, legally authenticated access route to Zenodo record and exact license/data dictionary; native binary paired decisions, original hash and pre-registered code, strong standards vs McMaster, Joel, Pronk, Ogushi and Matz; independently held-out venue/country only with domain harmonization verified.
